results.done: All 25 questions are registered, separated, independently verified and scored. (1) Separation by extract_candidate.py: model-visible requests (questions.json: id, shape, domain, question only), scorer-only keys/worked answers/wrong-answer examples (keys.json), and reference source documents (sources/) - the three-way split the command requires. (2) Independent verification by verify_keys.py: all 268 checks hold, exit 0 - 6 global checks (G1-G6), 195 per-question checks (Q1.1...Q25.7) and 67 cross-checks (X1-X67) that parse keys.json's own value strings and require agreement with the first-principles recomputation within the stated tolerances, so keys.json is the single source of key values. Every numerical key recomputed from first principles; dimensions, boundary operators (inclusive 'no more than', equality-permitted selections, strict regulatory thresholds), discrete selections and tolerance boundaries checked; all 56 claimed wrong answers falsified under the stated assumptions. (3) The five lookup questions (Q2, Q7, Q12, Q17, Q22) source-verified against four regulations: both 29 CFR 1910.146(b) oxygen definitions; 29 CFR 1910.95 Table G-16's 90/95/100 dBA rows (8, 4, 2 hours, slow response) and paragraph (g)'s audiometric provisions (baseline within 6 months, at least 14 hours workplace-noise-free, retest within 30 days); 40 CFR 141.62(b)'s maximum contaminant levels (fluoride 4.0 mg/L, nitrate 10 mg/L as nitrogen, arsenic 0.010 mg/L); 29 CFR 1910.147's attachment-means strength (no less than 50 pounds) and inspection frequency (at least annually). Every claimed verbatim quotation matched character-for-character against the archived July 1, 2014 annual editions (govinfo packages CFR-2014-title29-vol5 and CFR-2014-title40-vol23), editions identified by package identifier and GPO typesetting footer, not inferred from a current webpage; each regulation stability-cross-checked against the current eCFR as of 2026-10-01 (versioner API) - a 12-year span, satisfying the command's 'unchanged for at least three years' requirement. Twelve archive files (four govinfo PDFs, their four pdftotext extractions, and four eCFR snapshots), recorded as eight manifest archive records, are committed under sources/ with hashes, byte counts and retrieval dates in manifest.json. (4) The provider-free scorer (scorer.py) scores free-text answers against the keys with unit conversion and tolerance comparison, not regex presence: its self-test holds all 248 fixtures (25 model answers, 47 equivalent notations, 100 tolerance boundaries just inside and just past, 56 wrong answers, 20 discrete selections in both directions). (5) The suite guard tests/test_tier2_keys.py (17 tests) runs both instruments on the tree and proves each can fail on corrupted copies (convention 22): corrupted numeric key -> X1 fails; corrupted candidate export -> G1 fails; corrupted source archive -> Q2.1 fails; swapped model-answer steps -> Q5.5 fails; a corrupted key fails the intact model answer through the imported scorer; the version guard fails a one-byte change in any of the four versioned files. (6) The version record (versions.json, D44-style): the manifest's dataset_version/scorer_version name the current entry, and the guard checks all four versioned files (questions.json, keys.json, scorer.py, verify_keys.py) hash to it; each change to the four is a new entry naming the change and its trigger (the initial five-question registration, two instrument repairs, the complete 25-question registration at candidate-2026-10-03.3, and the freeze at frozen-2026-10-03). (7) The review checklist (evals/tier2/REVIEW.md) records every check and result, the four source records, the candidate provenance (the questions were authored by gpt-6.1-sol-pro with web_search/web_fetch/shell at the owner's direction - recorded as provenance, not a violation; no AI model was queried about the questions during verification), and the resolved signoff items. (8) The freeze the command orders after review: on 2026-10-03T21:41:20Z the owner ratified the tier-2 signoff ('ratify the tier-2 signoff'), covering the independent verification (all 268 checks) and the source review; the executor executed the freeze - manifest.json records frozen=true, an empty freeze_blocked_by, and the freeze record (grantor, time, scope, effect); the verifier's G3 check now requires the frozen state with the signoff recorded; both instruments' closing lines report the frozen version; extract_candidate.py (the manifest's generator) carries the freeze record so re-running it reproduces manifest.json byte-for-byte; versions.json carries the frozen-2026-10-03 entry (questions.json and keys.json hash identically to candidate-2026-10-03.3 - the freeze changed only what the instruments report and the manifest records, not the dataset content).
results.not_done: Nothing the command assigns to the executor remains. The command's acceptance criteria are met: the set is registered, separated, independently verified, scored, versioned, checklisted, and frozen on the owner's signoff. What remains is not this command's work: tier 3 (the five-arm experiment, ARCH-20261002-118) must obtain its own explicit ratifications before any paid run - the owner's ratification of the serving proposals (proposed models) and of the total spend authorization ($90.00 across 375 planned question-runs, an authorization ceiling, not a predicted cost). deviations.what: The command's stop clause ('If it is unavailable in your session, stop and request that exact array') fired at arrival and was honored; when the array arrived holding 5 questions, the executor did not stop again but registered the discrepancy as the freeze blocker; when the owner supplied the remaining 20 questions, the executor registered them verbatim without re-screening.
deviations.why: The stop clause exists to prevent regenerating or substituting questions. Every question registered is exactly what the owner supplied - nothing was regenerated, substituted, or model-produced. The count discrepancy was a hard ambiguity the command says to record before freezing; the owner's supply resolved it, and the resolution is itself recorded (the candidate hash changed and versions.json gained the candidate-2026-10-03.3 entry naming the trigger).

deviations.what: The owner supplied the remaining 20 questions in a malformed export file and authorized a JSON repair ('fix the json while your at it'); the executor repaired the syntax only.
deviations.why: The repair restored the export to valid JSON without altering, adding or removing any question content - the array the owner pasted is the array registered. The repaired file hashes to the manifest record (G1), and the extraction is idempotent (the suite guard re-runs extract_candidate.py on a copy and requires byte-identical outputs), so the registered dataset is a function of the repaired export alone.

deviations.what: Instrument repairs to verify_keys.py during the guard's construction (two version entries, candidate-2026-10-03.1 and .2).
deviations.why: The self-test did not print the fixture count it ran (convention 26: an instrument's report states what it measured), and the Q5 worked-answer checks read keys.json from the script's own directory even under --dir, so a corrupted copy could pass the ordering check against the original's model answer - the one path that ignored the directory it was told to verify. Both are instrument repairs (how reliably the instrument reaches a conclusion), not verdict-semantics changes; no check's meaning changed, and each repair is a versioned entry naming what changed and what triggered it.

deviations.what: The owner's 2026-10-03 instruction ('do tier 2 and 3, no stops, full permission to commit/push/merge') did not lift the command's hard input requirements or the freeze gate.
deviations.why: 'No stops' covered actions within the executor's authority (commit, push, merge on green). The freeze and any paid use remain gated on the owner or qualified-reviewer signoff the command requires; the set is registered unfrozen with the blocker recorded, which is the report the channel exists to produce.

deviations.what: The freeze changed the verifier's G3 check from requiring the unfrozen state (with a recorded blocker) to requiring the frozen state (with the owner's signoff recorded), and changed both instruments' closing lines.
